content:
**Visual observations from test image:**
- Corn ear with yellow/golden kernels (still plump, not mummified)
- White/grayish-white mold growing **between kernel rows** and over sections of the ear
- Some grayish discoloration at the tip area
- No pink/red, no olive-green, no dark green coloring
- Mold appears distributed across the ear surface

**Reasoning:**
- Eliminates Gibberella (pink-red mold at tip), Fusarium (salmon/pink cottony mold), Aspergillus (olive-green), Trichoderma (dark green)
- The white mycelium growing over and between kernels is the hallmark of **Diplodia ear rot**
- Reference collage confirms white mold on kernels with similar white mycelial growth pattern
- The test image appears to be an earlier stage before kernels become fully mummified/shrunken as seen in advanced Diplodia cases
